title: Product average for independent Boolean choices
statement: Let $r$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a_i:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\to\mathbb{R}$ for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$. For a uniformly chosen Boolean vector $\sigma\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}^r$, the average of $\prod_{i\in S}a_i(\sigma_i)$ equals $\prod_{i\in S}\frac{a_i(\mathrm{false})+a_i(\mathrm{true})}{2}$.
hypotheses_covered: For each coordinate $i$, $a_i$ is a real-valued function on the two Boolean values
$S$ is a subset of the $r$ coordinates
